title: Generics preserve relationships
summary: Write a generic helper that returns the first item or null without unsafe casts.

scenario.briefing: A campus API returns lists of different types. Write one typed helper that preserves the element type.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: The return type already permits null.
The first item is items[0], which may be undefined.
Use the nullish coalescing operator to supply null.

misconceptions.description: Using as T to silence the empty-array case.
misconceptions.feedback: A cast does not add a value. Use ?? null to represent absence honestly.

misconceptions.description: Falling back to any when a generic gets difficult.
misconceptions.feedback: any disables the relationship you are trying to preserve. Use a type parameter or a constrained generic.

sections.title: Type parameters preserve a relationship
sections.body: A generic function declares a type parameter that connects its inputs to its output: function first<T>(items: readonly T[]): T | undefined. The caller supplies the concrete type, or TypeScript infers it from the argument, so the result keeps the element type instead of widening to any or unknown.

sections.title: Constraints narrow what T may be
sections.body: A constraint limits which types a parameter accepts. <T, K extends keyof T> says that K must be one of T's property names, and the return type T[K] describes the value at that key. Constraints are checked at compile time and disappear from the emitted JavaScript.

sections.title: Generics do not validate runtime data
sections.body: A generic signature is a compile-time promise. JSON, localStorage, and network responses arrive as unknown values until a runtime guard checks them. Use a type parameter for relationships inside typed code and an explicit guard at the boundary.

vocabulary.definition: A type placeholder supplied by the caller of a generic function.
The compiler's deduction of a type from context.
A requirement that limits which types a type parameter may accept.
A type written T[K] that describes the value at key K of T.

steps.title: Return the first item or null
steps.prompt: Edit format.ts. firstOrNull<T> returns the first item or null when the array is empty.
hints: The return type already allows null.
items[0] is undefined for an empty array.
Use ?? to turn undefined into null.

steps.title: Generics and type safety

statements.label: A generic function can preserve the element type of its input.
A type assertion validates the runtime value.
T | null documents that absence is possible.
Using any is the safest way to generalize a helper.

steps.explanation: Generics carry the element type from input to output. A cast only tells the compiler to trust the author; it does not check the value.
hints: A cast does not check a runtime value.
any discards the relationship between input and output.
